# Judges Chapter 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_pages_287-288.jpg

1. In those days there was no king in Yisrael. And in those days the tribe of the Daniy was seeking for itself an inheritance to dwell [in], for there had not fallen to it until that day among the tribes of Yisrael an inheritance.

2. And the sons of Dan sent from their clan five men from their extremities, men — sons of valor — from Tsorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to search it. And they said to them, "Go, search the land." And they came to the hill-country of Ephrayim, to the house of Mikhah, and they lodged there.

3. They [were] near the house of Mikhah, and they recognized the voice of the young man, the Levite. And they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here, and what are you doing in this [place], and what [is it] to you here?"

4. And he said to them, "Thus and so Mikhah has done for me, and he has hired me, and I have become his priest."

5. And they said to him, "Inquire, please, of God, that we may know whether our way on which we are going will be prosperous."

6. And the priest said to them, "Go in peace. Before YHWH [is] your way on which you are going."

7. And the five men went and came to Layish. And they saw the people who [were] in its midst, dwelling securely, according to the custom of the Tsidonians, quiet and trusting, and there was no one possessing restraint humiliating [any] thing in the land, and they [were] far from the Tsidonians, and they had no dealings with anyone.

8. And they came to their brothers, to Tsorah and Eshtaol. And their brothers said to them, "What [do] you [say]?"

9. And they said, "Arise, and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, [it is] very good. And you are sitting still? Do not be sluggish to go, to enter to possess the land.

10. "When you go, you will come to a people trusting, and the land [is] wide on both sides, for God has given it into your hand — a place where there is no lack of any thing that [is] in the earth."

11. And there set out from there, from the clan of the Daniy, from Tsorah and from Eshtaol, six hundred men girded [with] weapons of war.

12. And they went up and camped at Qiryat-Yearim in Y'hudah. Therefore they called that place Machaneh-Dan until this day. Behold, [it is] behind Qiryat-Yearim.

13. And they passed from there [to] the hill-country of Ephrayim, and they came to the house of Mikhah.

14. And the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Layish answered and said to their brothers, "Do you know that there is in these houses an ephod and teraphim and a carved image and a cast image? And now, know what you shall do."

15. And they turned aside there and came to the house of the young man, the Levite, to the house of Mikhah, and they asked [about] his welfare.

16. And the six hundred men girded [with] their weapons of war, who [were] of the sons of Dan, were standing at the entrance of the gate.

17. And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up — they went in there — they took the carved image and the ephod and the teraphim and the cast image. And the priest was standing at the entrance of the gate, and the six hundred men girded [with] weapons of war.

18. And these went into the house of Mikhah and took the carved image, the ephod, and the teraphim, and the cast image. And the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

19. And they said to him, "Be silent! Put your hand over your mouth and come with us and be to us a father and a priest. Is it better for you to be a priest to the house of one man, or to be a priest to a tribe and to a clan in Yisrael?"

20. And the heart of the priest was glad, and he took the ephod and the teraphim and the carved image, and he came into the midst of the people.

21. And they turned and went, and they put the little ones and the livestock and the valuables before them.

22. They had gone far from the house of Mikhah, and the men who [were] in the houses that [were] near the house of Mikhah were called together, and they overtook the sons of Dan.

23. And they called out to the sons of Dan. And they turned their faces and said to Mikhah, "What [is it] to you that you have been called together?"

24. And he said, "My gods that I made you have taken away, and the priest, and you have gone. And what [is it] to me still? And what [is] this you say to me, 'What [is it] to you?'"

25. And the sons of Dan said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, lest men bitter of soul fall upon you, and you lose your life and the lives of your household."

26. And the sons of Dan went on their way. And Mikhah saw that they [were] stronger than he, and he turned and went back to his house.

27. And they took what Mikhah had made and the priest who had been his, and they came against Layish, against a people quiet and trusting, and they struck them with the edge of the sword. And the city they burned with fire.

28. And there was no deliverer, for it [was] far from Tsidon, and they had no dealings with anyone, and it [was] in the valley that [belongs] to Beit-R'chov. And they built the city and dwelt in it.

29. And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Yisrael. But Layish [was] the name of the city at first.

30. And the sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image. And Y'honatan son of Gershom son of M'nashsheh — he and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Daniy — until the day of the exile of the land.

31. And they set up for themselves the carved image of Mikhah that he had made, all the days that the house of God was in Shiloh.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.1 — "there was no king in Israel":** The refrain from 17:6, here without its second clause ("everyone did what was right in his own eyes"). The abbreviated form introduces the Danite migration as a consequence of the kingless chaos.

2. **v.7 — "quiet and trusting" (shoqet uvoteach):** The pair describes a people living in peaceful security — militarily unprepared, without suspicion of danger. The description functions as the narrator's implicit moral judgment: the Danites exploit innocence.

3. **v.17 — fourfold sacred objects:** pesel (carved image), ephod, teraphim, massekah (cast image) — all four are listed together in vv.14, 17, 18, and 20. The repetition hammers home the comprehensiveness of the theft: they took everything.

4. **v.30 — "son of M'nashsheh" (ben M'nashsheh):** The Leningrad Codex writes מְנַשֶּׁה with a suspended nun (נ) — the letter nun is raised above the line. The consonants m-n-sh-h spell "Manasseh," but the raised nun signals that the original reading was m-sh-h — "Mosheh" (Moses). This is the most famous scribal emendation in the Hebrew Bible: a scribe inserted nun to change "Moses" to "Manasseh," protecting the reputation of Moses by disguising the fact that his own grandson became an idolatrous priest. EMET preserves the MT consonantal text (M'nashsheh) but notes the original reading.

5. **v.30 — "until the day of the exile of the land":** galot ha'arets — which "exile"? Options include the Assyrian conquest of the north (722 BCE), the Philistine capture of the ark (1 Samuel 4), or a localized event. The phrase stands in tension with v.31, which ties the idolatry to "all the days the house of God was in Shiloh" — a shorter period. The two verses may reflect different editorial layers.

— EMET, AI Translator
